newsitem.title: USA: Tech rally, Greenspan push Nasdaq to new high.
newsitem.headline: Tech rally, Greenspan push Nasdaq to new high.

text.p: Nasdaq shares set a new record Tuesday as technology stocks rallied ahead of International Business Machines Corp's fourth quarter earnings report, which were released after the market closed.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's upbeat assessment of the economy also lifted the market, traders said.

"IBM traded high during the day, driving techs higher... and Greenspan didn't say anything too damaging," said Nelson Gold, senior vice president of over-the-counter trading at Interstate-Johnson Lane Corp.

The Nasdaq Composite Index gained 12.70 points or 0.93 percent to close unofficially at 1376.98, a new record that topped Monday's record of 1364.28. The Dow industrials climbed 40 points to an unofficial close of 6884. The long bond gained 18/32 to yield 6.78 percent.

Nasdaq gain was led by Microsoft Corp, which added 4-1/4 to 95 in heavy trading. Intel Corp gained 2-13/16 to 148-1/16 and Sun Microsystems Inc increased one to 33-3/8. Shares of Target Therapeutics Inc also rose 11-1/4 to 70-1/4 on news it would be acquired by Boston Scientific Corp.
